title: Settlement
description: A place people live, at the scale between a region and a point of interest. What a player can walk into is a `field_map` or a `poi`; this is the thing those refer back to.

aliases.description: Other names this has been known by. Added when `Dwarka` became `North Dwarka`: canon held one Dwarka and then held several, and a rename that drops the old name breaks every reference written before it.

epoch_founded.description: An epoch id. Checked by the epoch pass, which matches any field whose *name* mentions an epoch -- this one is why that rule is written the way it is.

canon.description: How firmly this is established. `primary` is stated by the source material, `inferred` is a reading canon has committed to.

within.description:
What contains this place -- another place, a region, a settlement or a field map.

Exists because canon names far more places than it can survey. Seventeen were named by events and drawn nowhere, because only the ones legible on `dump/Partial_map.png` ever got coordinates and everything authored since has had none. Each era's chapter mentioned places the era's map did not show.

Plotting each by hand does not scale and mostly invents geography. This does neither: the Nilgiri Canopy is in the Nilgiri, the Narmada University Library is on the Narmada field map, and saying so is a fact canon already holds. The atlas resolves a position from the parent and **draws it as inherited rather than surveyed** -- a hollow marker, not a filled one -- so the map never claims a precision it does not have.

A place with its own `coordinates` ignores this. A place with neither is simply unplaced, which stays honest and common.

epochs.description: Epoch ids from database/timeline/epochs.json. Absent means the place exists in every era.
